claim_text: LIMA, a 65B parameter LLaMa model fine-tuned on only 1,000 carefully curated prompts and responses without reinforcement learning or human preference modeling, demonstrates remarkably strong performance.
evidence_quote: LIMA demonstrates remarkably strong performance, learning to follow specific response formats from only a handful of examples in the training data

claim_text: Responses from LIMA are either equivalent or strictly preferred to GPT-4 in 43% of cases in a controlled human study.
evidence_quote: responses from LIMA are either equivalent or strictly preferred to GPT-4 in 43% of cases

claim_text: LIMA outperforms RLHF-trained DaVinci003 from OpenAI in human preference.
evidence_quote: LIMA outperforms RLHF-trained DaVinci003 from OpenAI

claim_text: LIMA produces equal or preferable responses compared to Bard in 58% of cases.
evidence_quote: this statistic is as high as 58% when compared to Bard

claim_text: Almost all knowledge in large language models is learned during pretraining, and only limited instruction tuning data is necessary to teach models to produce high quality output.
evidence_quote: almost all knowledge in large language models is learned during pretraining, and only limited instruction tuning data is necessary to teach models to produce high quality output

claim_text: The Superficial Alignment Hypothesis states that a model's knowledge and capabilities are learnt almost entirely during pretraining, while alignment teaches it which subdistribution of formats should be used when interacting with users.
evidence_quote: A model's knowledge and capabilities are learnt almost entirely during pretraining, while alignment teaches it which subdistribution of formats should be used when interacting with users.

claim_text: LIMA can conduct coherent multi-turn dialogue despite having zero dialogue examples in the training set.
evidence_quote: despite having zero dialogue examples, we find that LIMA can conduct coherent multi-turn dialogue

claim_text: Adding only 30 hand-crafted dialogue chains to the training set dramatically improves LIMA's multi-turn dialogue ability.
evidence_quote: this ability can be dramatically improved by adding only 30 hand-crafted dialogue chains to the training set

claim_text: Ablation experiments reveal vastly diminishing returns when scaling up data quantity without also scaling up prompt diversity.
evidence_quote: vastly diminishing returns when scaling up data quantity without also scaling up prompt diversity

claim_text: Scaling up input diversity and output quality have measurable positive effects on alignment, while scaling up quantity alone might not.
evidence_quote: scaling up input diversity and output quality have measurable positive effects, while scaling up quantity alone might not

claim_text: LIMA responds safely to 80% of 30 potentially sensitive prompts from the test set.
evidence_quote: LIMA responds safely to 80% of them (including 6 out of 10 prompts with malicious intent)

claim_text: 50% of LIMA's outputs are considered excellent in an absolute assessment.
evidence_quote: 50% of LIMA answers are considered excellent

claim_text: LIMA achieves similar absolute performance statistics outside of its training distribution, suggesting it generalizes well.
evidence_quote: LIMA achieves similar absolute performance statistics outside of its training distribution, suggesting that it is able to generalize well

claim_text: Perplexity does not correlate with generation quality for LIMA.
evidence_quote: We find that perplexity does not correlate with generation quality

claim_text: GPT-4 as an annotator achieves agreement with humans on par with human-human agreement for this preference task.
evidence_quote: GPT-4 on-par in agreement with human annotators, essentially passing the Turking Test for this task

claim_text: Imitation models fine-tuned on broad-coverage ChatGPT outputs do not improve (or even decline) on evaluation tasks that are not heavily supported in the imitation data.
evidence_quote: ShareGPT-mix imitation models do not improve (or even decline) in accuracy as compared to the base model, even when adding additional imitation data
source_section: 4.3 Targeted Automatic Evaluations Expose Failure Modes

claim_text: Training imitation models on task-specific data (NQ-synthetic) substantially closes the gap to ChatGPT on that task.
evidence_quote: the NQ-Synthetic models substantially close the gap to ChatGPT on NQ, showing that local imitation of a model is far more feasible in practice
source_section: 4.3 Targeted Automatic Evaluations Expose Failure Modes

claim_text: Increasing the base model size (from 1.5B to 13B) leads to substantial accuracy improvements on benchmarks, whereas increasing imitation data amount does not.
evidence_quote: scaling up the base LM steadily improves results, suggesting that the key difference between open-source and closed-source LMs is a raw capabilities gap
source_section: 4.3 Targeted Automatic Evaluations Expose Failure Modes

claim_text: Crowdworkers rate imitation model outputs as competitive with ChatGPT, with ~70% of outputs rated equal or better.
evidence_quote: Crowdworkers initially rate the quality of our imitation models highly, as ~70% of their outputs are rated as equal or better than those of ChatGPT

claim_text: Imitation models learn to mimic ChatGPT's style (length, word choice, authoritative tone, list structure) but not its factuality.
evidence_quote: imitation models perform well according to human evaluations because they are adept at mimicking ChatGPT's style—they output fluent, confident, and well-structured answers

claim_text: Imitation models inherit the safety and toxicity guidelines of the teacher model, becoming less toxic on RealToxicityPrompts as more imitation data is added.

claim_text: Broadly matching ChatGPT using weaker base LMs would require an extremely large and diverse imitation dataset, far closer to the scale of pretraining.

claim_text: Training on more broad-coverage imitation data can hurt performance on some benchmarks compared to the base model, due to distribution shift.

source_section: 4.3 Targeted Automatic Evaluations Expose Failure Modes

claim_text: GPT-4 evaluations show the same trends as crowdworker evaluations, but with a slightly larger absolute preference for ChatGPT's outputs.

claim_text: Model imitation is effective when one has a powerful base LM and wants to avoid annotating expensive finetuning data.

claim_text: Llama 2 is a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned large language models ranging in scale from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters.
evidence_quote: we develop and release Llama 2, a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) ranging in scale from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters.

claim_text: Llama 2-Chat models outperform open-source chat models on most benchmarks tested.
evidence_quote: Our models outperform open-source chat models on most benchmarks we tested
applies_to: Llama 2-Chat models vs open-source chat models

claim_text: Llama 2-Chat may be a suitable substitute for closed-source models based on human evaluations for helpfulness and safety.
evidence_quote: based on our human evaluations for helpfulness and safety, may be a suitable substitute for closed-source models.

claim_text: Llama 2 was trained on 2 trillion tokens of data from publicly available sources, excluding Meta's products or services.
evidence_quote: We trained on 2 trillion tokens of data as this provides a good performance–cost trade-off

claim_text: Llama 2 uses grouped-query attention (GQA) for the 34B and 70B models to improve inference scalability.
evidence_quote: Bigger models — 34B and 70B — use Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) for improved inference scalability.

claim_text: Llama 2 has a context length of 4096 tokens, doubled from Llama 1's 2048 tokens.
evidence_quote: Llama 2: Context Length 4k; Llama 1: Context Length 2k

claim_text: Llama 2 70B improves MMLU and BBH results by approximately 5 and 8 points respectively compared to Llama 1 65B.
evidence_quote: Llama 2 70B improves the results on MMLU and BBH by ≈5 and ≈8 points, respectively, compared to Llama 1 65B.

claim_text: Llama 2 70B is close to GPT-3.5 on MMLU and GSM8K but has a significant gap on coding benchmarks.
evidence_quote: Llama 2 70B is close to GPT-3.5 (OpenAI, 2023) on MMLU and GSM8K, but there is a significant gap on coding benchmarks.

claim_text: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with 27,540 high-quality annotations was sufficient to achieve high-quality results for Llama 2-Chat.
evidence_quote: We stopped annotating SFT after collecting a total of 27,540 annotations.

claim_text: Using fewer but higher-quality SFT examples from vendor-based annotation improved results over using millions of third-party examples.
evidence_quote: By setting aside millions of examples from third-party datasets and using fewer but higher-quality examples from our own vendor-based annotation efforts, our results notably improved.

claim_text: RLHF for Llama 2-Chat uses binary comparison protocol for human preference data collection, focusing on helpfulness and safety.
evidence_quote: We chose a binary comparison protocol over other schemes, mainly because it enables us to maximize the diversity of collected prompts.

claim_text: Llama 2-Chat uses Ghost Attention (GAtt) to help control dialogue flow over multiple turns.
evidence_quote: We also share a new technique, Ghost Attention (GAtt), which we find helps control dialogue flow over multiple turns

claim_text: Llama 2 70B outperforms all open-source models on grouped academic benchmarks.
evidence_quote: Llama 2 70B model outperforms all open-source models.

claim_text: Llama 2-Chat models generally perform better than existing open-source models on helpfulness and safety benchmarks.
evidence_quote: Llama 2-Chat models generally perform better than existing open-source models.

claim_text: DPO can fine-tune LMs to align with human preferences as well as or better than existing methods.
evidence_quote: Our experiments show that DPO can fine-tune LMs to align with human preferences as well as or better than existing methods.
applies_to: LMs up to 6B parameters, sentiment modulation, summarization, dialogue

claim_text: DPO exceeds PPO-based RLHF in ability to control sentiment of generations.
evidence_quote: Notably, fine-tuning with DPO exceeds PPO-based RLHF in ability to control sentiment of generations

claim_text: DPO matches or improves response quality in summarization and single-turn dialogue while being substantially simpler to implement and train.
evidence_quote: matches or improves response quality in summarization and single-turn dialogue while being substantially simpler to implement and train.

claim_text: DPO eliminates the need for sampling from the LM during fine-tuning or performing significant hyperparameter tuning.
evidence_quote: eliminating the need for sampling from the LM during fine-tuning or performing significant hyperparameter tuning.

claim_text: DPO implicitly optimizes the same objective as existing RLHF algorithms (reward maximization with a KL-divergence constraint) but is simple to implement and straightforward to train.
evidence_quote: We propose Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), an algorithm that implicitly optimizes the same objective as existing RLHF algorithms (reward maximization with a KL-divergence constraint) but is simple to implement and straightforward to train.

claim_text: The DPO update increases the relative log probability of preferred to dispreferred responses, incorporating a dynamic, per-example importance weight that prevents model degeneration.
evidence_quote: Intuitively, the DPO update increases the relative log probability of preferred to dispreferred responses, but it incorporates a dynamic, per-example importance weight that prevents the model degeneration that we find occurs with a naive probability ratio objective.

claim_text: DPO uses a change of variables to define the preference loss as a function of the policy directly, given a dataset of human preferences over model responses.
evidence_quote: DPO uses a change of variables to define the preference loss as a function of the policy directly.

claim_text: DPO provides the highest expected reward for all KL values in the IMDb sentiment generation task.
evidence_quote: DPO provides the highest expected reward for all KL values, demonstrating the quality of the optimization.

claim_text: DPO exceeds PPO's best-case performance on TL;DR summarization, while being more robust to changes in the sampling temperature.
evidence_quote: DPO exceeds PPO's best-case performance on summarization, while being more robust to changes in the sampling temperature.

claim_text: DPO is the only method that improves over chosen summaries in the Anthropic-HH test set.
evidence_quote: DPO is the only method that improves over chosen summaries in the Anthropic-HH test set.

claim_text: The gradient of the DPO loss increases the likelihood of preferred completions and decreases the likelihood of dispreferred completions, weighted by how incorrectly the implicit reward model orders the completions.
evidence_span: Section 4, What does the DPO update do?
evidence_quote: Intuitively, the gradient of the loss function LDPO increases the likelihood of the preferred completions yw and decreases the likelihood of dispreferred completions yl. Importantly, the examples are weighed by how much higher the implicit reward model r̂θ rates the dispreferred completions
source_section: Section 4, What does the DPO update do?

claim_text: A naïve version of DPO without the weighting coefficient can cause the language model to degenerate.
evidence_span: Section 4, What does the DPO update do?
evidence_quote: Our experiments suggest the importance of this weighting, as a naïve version of this method without the weighting coefficient can cause the language model to degenerate (Appendix Table 3).
source_section: Section 4, What does the DPO update do?

claim_text: Under the Plackett-Luce and Bradley-Terry preference frameworks, two reward functions from the same equivalence class induce the same preference distribution.
evidence_quote: Under the Plackett-Luce, and in particular the Bradley-Terry, preference framework, two reward functions from the same class induce the same preference distribution.

claim_text: Two reward functions from the same equivalence class induce the same optimal policy under the constrained RL problem.
evidence_quote: Two reward functions from the same equivalence class induce the same optimal policy under the constrained RL problem.

claim_text: All reward classes consistent with the Plackett-Luce (and Bradley-Terry) models can be represented with the reparameterization r(x,y) = β log π(y|x)/πref(y|x) for some model π and given reference model πref.
evidence_quote: Under mild assumptions, all reward classes consistent with the Plackett-Luce (and Bradley-Terry in particular) models can be represented with the reparameterization r(x,y) = β log π(y|x)/πref(y|x) for some model π(y|x) and a given reference model πref(y|x).
applies_to: Theoretical, all Plackett-Luce and Bradley-Terry models
